sections.subtitle: Match context
sections.text: Arsenal welcome Newcastle United to the Emirates Stadium. Arsenal are 2nd (70 points) and still in the title race; Newcastle are 14th (42 points). Modelling points towards a home win, with both teams to score close to a coin flip.

sections.subtitle: Current form
sections.text: Arsenal are 1-1-3 in their last 5 but led the expected goals in all 5 matches, suggesting results have lagged finishing. Newcastle are 1-0-4 and have allowed high expected goals against in their last 4 defeats (2.99, 2.56, 2.44, 4.29).

sections.subtitle: Head-to-head
sections.text: Arsenal have won the last 2 meetings (3-2, 2-1). Newcastle scored first in both of those matches, but Arsenal finished stronger. Corners have often been high in this fixture.

sections.subtitle: Season stats and tactical notes
sections.text: Arsenal’s defence is league-best (26 conceded, 15 clean sheets). They create a high volume of big chances (99) but conversion is middling and they underperform expected goals (-6.1). Set-pieces are a weapon (14 headers scored, 1st). Newcastle’s goal difference is 46-49 and they score late (76-90: 38.8% of league goals), which aligns with Arsenal also strong late scorers (76-90: 15).

sections.subtitle: Key players
sections.text: For Arsenal, Declan Rice drives chance creation (62 key passes, 16 big chances created) and Bukayo Saka offers 1.8 successful dribbles per match. Gabriel Magalhães has been robust in duels (70.8% won) and excelled in the last head-to-head. For Newcastle, Bruno Guimarães is the main threat (9 goals, high influence), but absences for Anthony Gordon, Joelinton and Fabian Schär weaken both ends.

sections.subtitle: Referee, cards and corners
sections.text: Samuel Barrott averages 3.8 yellows per match and very few reds (0.06). Team streaks lean under for cards, while head-to-head often runs high on corners. Expect a moderate card count and corners around the 10–11 mark.

sections.subtitle: Match prediction
sections.text: Arsenal to control territory and chances, with their defence likely to limit Newcastle’s undermanned attack. The visitors’ late threat is a factor, but the model and underlying numbers favour a home win. Lean towards Arsenal to win, with both teams to score slightly less likely than not.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match context
halftimeSections.text: Arsenal lead 1-0 at the interval at Emirates Stadium after Eberechi Eze finished early from a Kai Havertz assist. Possession is level (50-50) and the general flow has been balanced, but Newcastle United have fashioned the clearer opening and carry aerial superiority. The match is finely poised with small margins deciding the first half.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Key first-half stats
halftimeSections.text: Underlying numbers favour a Newcastle response: expected goals Arsenal 0.08 vs Newcastle 0.33; shots on target 2-2; big chances created 0-1 (Newcastle missed); penalty area entries 9-14 to Newcastle; final third entries 30-29; possessions won in the final third 3-4 to Newcastle. In duels, Newcastle lead (overall 51% won; aerial 75%). Corners are 3-1 to Arsenal.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Tactical patterns and momentum
halftimeSections.text: Arsenal started on the front foot, then turned a strong spell into the opener. Newcastle wrestled control through the middle of the half with sustained territory and entries into the box. Another away-side surge arrived around the half-hour, before a quieter close where Newcastle still edged the initiative. Arsenal’s threat has come when they speed up wide combinations and find Eze between the lines; Newcastle look most dangerous when they progress quickly into the inside channels and attack early crosses.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Player notes
halftimeSections.text: For Arsenal, Eze took his chance well and Noni Madueke tested the goalkeeper once. Martin Odegaard and Havertz each produced a key pass, with Havertz also registering the assist. Martín Zubimendi provided control and defensive work (2 tackles won, 2 clearances), while Piero Hincapié stepped in aggressively (2 tackles won). For Newcastle, Bruno Guimarães has been the main supplier (2 key passes). Joe Willock timed runs well (1 shot on target, 1 chance created), and William Osula missed the half’s big chance. At the back, Sven Botman read play effectively (4 interceptions, 3 clearances) with Malick Thiaw and Dan Burn adding presence in the air.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Second-half outlook
halftimeSections.text: Given Newcastle’s edge in box entries and aerials, expect more early crosses and set-piece targeting of Burn and Botman. Willock’s late Box 18 arrivals remain a key route. Arsenal will try to slow the game with Zubimendi and Declan Rice, then spring wide via Madueke and Eze to isolate full-backs. Viktor Gyökeres has been quiet; sharper near-post runs and earlier deliveries could bring him into the game. If Arsenal cannot improve first-contact success on defensive crosses, Newcastle’s pressure is likely to tell at some point.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Cards and corners
halftimeSections.text: No bookings are recorded in the data so far. With duels slightly in Newcastle’s favour and more aerial contests expected, a few second-half cautions are plausible. Corners should continue to accumulate, with Newcastle’s set-pieces a genuine route to goal despite Arsenal leading the corner count 3-1 at the break.

halftimeSections.subtitle: Match prediction
halftimeSections.text: The numbers point towards a Newcastle equaliser, most likely from a second-phase cross or a late midfield run. Arsenal’s counter threat remains, but if the pattern holds, a shared outcome is the likeliest result. Predicted outcome: 1-1, with Newcastle scoring the next goal in the second half.
